summary: Implemented the FAWE-side PolymerEditBridge against Polymer's now-accepted public bulk-edit API and added an explicit direct-section route discriminator. The Fabric module compiles, packages, and compiles the bridge against the exact polymer-common jar nested in the accepted Polymer bundle. No native FAWE S7 integration suite was run, so full S7 remains unaccepted.

discoveryTopology.reason: isModLoaded("polymer-core") is true; common is on core's runtime classpath; core and VE participants are present.

The bundle is the only supported install for this stage. A common-only deployment contains no PolymerBlock mappings (core) and no BlockWithElementHolder API (VE), so no Polymer state or holders can exist and a token would have nothing to reconcile. The bridge's absence is therefore safe, not a reconciliation gap.

VE depends only on common, so core-free VE deployments are valid and holders can exist. EditIntegrations.directSectionRouteSupported() returns false in this topology, so FabricCommitCoordinator disables whole-section publication and every cell goes through the ordinary lifecycle path (vanilla setBlockState hooks run). The bridge stays fail-closed, but holders cannot silently go stale. Any-of discovery (polymer-core OR polymer-virtual-entity) remains future work; the current Map<mod, impl> shape would double-register the same provider id and trip validate().

sourceChanges.summary: Owner-thread Polymer reservation: detached construction, prepare only for the direct-section route, reconcile actual committed changes against the FAWE receipt, publish after lighting and recipient sends, close exactly once on the owner thread, and refuse off-thread discard of a live token. Prepare refusals fail before any write with explicit no-writes/reload guidance. Non-block payloads never acquire a token.

Added a provider veto, allowsDirectSections(level, authorized), and a route-aware beforePublication(level, authorized, directSections). The legacy two-argument hook remains source-compatible, is now default-empty, and is delegated to by the three-argument default.

Added owner-thread directSectionEligible (BLOCK only, no block entity on either side, one loaded chunk, minecraft-namespace-only sections) and made writeUnit take an explicit route. The strict route rechecks lifecycle cells, refuses lost eligibility, and never silently falls back while a provider holds section-scoped state; the ordinary route writes every cell through the existing lifecycle path.

Computes the direct-section route after authorization, requires EditIntegrations.directSectionRouteSupported() (VE-without-core guard), requires every reservation to allow it, passes the route to beforePublication, and passes it to writeUnit. Native/WNA mutations never enter the direct-section route or acquire a Polymer token.

Added directSectionRouteSupported(): whole-section publication is disabled when polymer-virtual-entity is installed without polymer-core, because holders can exist while the bridge is not discovered. The guard forces the ordinary per-cell lifecycle, which still runs vanilla setBlockState hooks.

Added `fawepublish stats`, returning FabricEdits.publicationStatistics() as JSON. The combined S7 probe uses it to prove the direct-section route ran (sections incremented, fallbackWrites unchanged) instead of inferring the route from world state.
Compile-time signature mirror of the accepted public API. The mirror is a separate source set, never packaged, and not on the runtime classpath; real classes come from polymer-common at runtime.
Wired the polymerApiStub source set into compileJava as compileOnly output and made compileJava depend on the stub classes.

routeSemantics: Preparation remains detached and performs no live chunk or Polymer API access.
The coordinator authorizes every delta, then checks the static route-support guard and computes directSectionEligible over the whole final authorized set.

The static guard disables the direct-section route when polymer-virtual-entity is installed without polymer-core, because holders can exist while the bridge is not discovered; ordinary per-cell writes still run the vanilla lifecycle hooks.
If eligible, every reservation is consulted through allowsDirectSections; any false veto forces the ordinary per-cell route for the entire proposal.
The direct route acquires the Polymer token in beforePublication, replaces whole sections without calling LevelChunk.setBlockState, and does not mix ordinary or native writes while the token is live.

A prepare refusal (unsupported attachment, Immersive Portals, reserved/quarantined chunk, or unloaded chunk) fails the unit before any write with an explicit no-writes message. The operation is not retried and the coordinator never switches routes mid-publication; unload/reload is required when the chunk is quarantined or no longer the loaded instance.
Non-block and lifecycle-heavy proposals do not acquire a Polymer token; they remain transparent to Polymer.
Polymer refuses more than sixteen sections; FAWE vetoes the direct route before prepare in that case.
contractAdherence: prepare(LevelChunk, Set<Integer>, Map<BlockPos, BlockState>) is called on the owner thread immediately before the non-yielding direct-section writes, using the exact loaded chunk, absolute section Y numbers, and immutable proposed native states.
No yield occurs between prepare, section installation, and token.reconcile; reconcile is invoked even for partial applied results.

token.reconcile() returns Polymer's independently observed actual changes; the bridge compares them with CommitReceipt.applied() by position, state id, and canonical NBT. Disagreement is a finalization failure and is never retried.
The bridge strips Polymer's keepPacked marker before comparing block-entity NBT so the comparison matches FAWE's full-metadata receipt payload.
Lighting is awaited through FabricWorldAccess.completePublication before token.publish(). token.publish() runs on the owner thread after that wait.
token.close() is called exactly once on the owner thread from the coordinator's finish path; successful publication is idempotent.
A live token cannot reach off-thread discard; discard refuses it. Shutdown before publication closes on the owner thread.
The bridge uses only the public API surface described by handoff/s7-polymer/api-contract.json; no Polymer private holder map or mixin state is reflected.

harnessNotes: Minecraft 26.3 dedicated servers default white-list=true; non-op test clients must run with white-list=false (FAWE S6 smoke already sets this).
Polymer's accepted harness fixes were test-only: white-list=false and re-adding forceload after pendingreload so recorded holder IDs stay valid for the rejoin client.

Combined S7 probe plan: install the FAWE dist + testmod + fabric-api alongside the accepted Polymer bundle, launch with -Dfawe.experimental.coordinated=true, place oak_log via setblock, and run /fawe-coordinated set minecraft:air on a 1x1x1 selection. A reconciled bridge detaches the VE holder and the client display disappears; a bypassed bridge leaves the display attached. Re-place oak_log and set stripped_oak_log to assert holder identity retention. `fawepublish stats` must show sections +1 with fallbackWrites unchanged.
The combined probe is not a full S7 acceptance run; it exercises one direct-section edit and one identity-retention edit with the installed bundle.
residualGaps: Full S7 remains unaccepted. The Polymer API part is accepted at a0ce5b32 (bundle e5251e9f...), but FAWE has no native S7 integration suite, no combined S7/earlier-stage regression, and no consumer adapters.
No native FAWE S7 integration suite ran. This environment lacks TMPDIR, VK_DRIVER_FILES, Xvfb, and xauth; the Gradle test task is NO-SOURCE and does not exercise the Polymer route.

test/candidate-manifest.json still stages polymer-bundled 0.18.5-rkc.4, not the accepted 0.18.6-fawe-s7.1 bundle, so the existing native harness would not test this API even if its display prerequisites were available.

VE-without-core is guarded but not natively exercised: polymer-virtual-entity depends only on polymer-common, so core-free VE deployments are valid and holders can exist while the bridge is not discovered. EditIntegrations.directSectionRouteSupported() now forces the ordinary per-cell lifecycle in that topology, so vanilla setBlockState hooks run and holders cannot silently go stale. Any-of discovery (polymer-core OR polymer-virtual-entity) remains future work because the current Map<mod, impl> shape would double-register the same provider id and trip validate().

A prepare refusal (unsupported attachment/Immersive Portals, reserved/quarantined chunk, or unloaded chunk) fails the unit before any write with an explicit no-writes/reload message. FAWE deliberately does not fall back to the ordinary route in this revision; no untracked writes or retries occur.

If reading an actual after-value throws after a mutation, FAWE's receipt may under-report applied deltas. Polymer's token would still quarantine the chunk, but FAWE's own quarantine set might not learn about the changed chunk from an empty applied list.
No FAWE-side negative-control, ordering, recipient, lighting, disconnect, or unload tests exist for this bridge. The coordinator and test probes were not extended for the Polymer route.
Consumer-owned adapters (chests, portals, portable attachment/history codecs, diagonal walls, Terraform, shaded kalic0re data) remain separate work and are not implemented here.
The compile-time mirror is manual and currently matches the accepted API. Replace it with the real dependency once the accepted artifact is published or staged.
Full S7 acceptance, combined S7 plus earlier-stage regressions, and S12 consumer/visual acceptance remain open.
